items.title: Government Funding Pressure On Iran War, National Security & Tech, Iowa Detonation
items.summary: Democrats are weighing whether to use the government funding deadline to cut off money for the war in Iran, exposing divisions over how quickly the party should act. The Trump administration approved sales of advanced U.S. chips to Chinese companies, including some the Pentagon has linked to China’s military, fueling a debate over whether those sales help America compete or create new security risks. The Army delayed plans to destroy thousands of pounds of unstable bomb-making material in Iowa after public pressure and a lawsuit, even as officials warn colder weather could make it more dangerous. items.title: Melania: the series review – so bad it robbed me of my capacity to discern time and space
items.summary: The first lady’s two-part TV documentary is a dead-eyed advert that barely manages to masquerade as entertainment. Calling it thin gruel would be an insult to the gruel industry Previously on Melania: earlier this year – either because it found her a compelling subject, or because it wanted to flatter the president before a potentially destructive upcoming antitrust trial – Amazon spent $75m (£57m) to make and market a theatrically released documentary about Melania Trump. I’m telling you this for two reasons. First, because you didn’t watch the Melania film. Nobody did, except for journalists who sat in otherwise empty cinemas and (if reports are to believed) people who responded to Craigslist ads offering them $50 to see it. The second reason is because Melania is a series now. Continue reading...

items.title: Grand Theft Auto fans skip work and pull all-nighters to play new instalment
items.summary: Hotly anticipated Bonnie and Clyde-inspired adventure GTA VI has gamers glued to their screens around the world Grand Theft Auto fans around the world pulled all-nighters, skipped work and school, and attended overnight launch parties to vicariously embark on police chases and coordinate robberies as the latest instalment of the eagerly anticipated series arrived. GTA VI, a Bonnie and Clyde-inspired crime adventure game set in the fictional US state of Leonida, was launched at midnight on Wednesday after a 13-year wait. Continue reading...

items.title: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse
items.summary: Week-long efforts fail to establish negotiating mandate on AI warfare after Russian ‘filibustering’ Week-long efforts to agree a negotiating mandate for a legally binding international treaty to control the use of autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am after all-night talks failed to overcome Russian objections. Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option. Continue reading...

items.title: Pill to treat pancreatic cancer hailed as ‘biggest breakthrough in decades’
items.summary: Cancer undetectable for one in 12 patients in daraxonrasib trial, while nearly all participants’ tumours stopped growing A pill that can shrink and potentially eliminate pancreas tumours is being hailed as the biggest breakthrough treatment for the cancer in decades. In one in 12 of the patients given the drug, daraxonrasib , during a trial, the cancer became undetectable, and the tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 patients. The trial participants had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body. Continue reading...

items.body: Pseudoruminococcus massiliensis is a species of bacterium, which was first isolated from the gut microbiota of a healthy Senegalese faecal transplant donor. The bacterium was named after the French city of Marseille, where the strain was isolated in 2017. == Structure == P. massiliensis cells are cocci: they are spherical/round-shaped. The bacterium’s cells are 0.6x45 μm in size and non-motile (it is incapable of moving independently). P. massiliensis colonies are grey, smooth and transparent. Colonies are, on average, 0.2-1.5mm in diameter. When grown on a specific medium (GAM agar), the bacterium has been observed to form protrusions, which could be identified as pili or fimbriae: these appendages on the surface of the bacterium e.g. helps it attach to surfaces. Scientists suggest these protrusions could play a role in the successful colonization of P. massiliensis. The bacterium, however, does not adhere well to mucus and might therefore not be able to stick to the epithelium of the colon. == Phylogeny == The closest related species to P. massiliensis is Ruminococcus bromii. R. bromii is considered a keystone species within the human gut ecosystem. == References ==

items.title: Depraved art: a disturbing history
items.summary: For millennia, humans have created art with the power to shock, disturb and offend. But what makes an artwork truly dangerous? And should it ever be censored? From Hitler’s paintings to the racist caricatures of Jim Crow America, Daisy Dixon takes Jon Bauckham on a tour of history’s most depraved art, revealing both its capacity for cruelty and its use as a tool of oppression. Please note, this episode does contain explicit discussions of themes including sexual violence and racism.
